Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 12 Aug 2026 15:10:00 -0400
Subject: Proof of concept workshop — interactive prompt review & load test

Hi Alex,

Thanks again for the time last week — excited to get the hands-on workshop on the calendar. The goal for this session is to:

- Walk through a short set of representative prompts you shared
- Validate routing/response profiles for the 3 use cases (support triage, summary, long-form assist)
- Run a light load test on a sample prompt to check latency and KV cache behavior

Proposed 90-minute slots (all in ET):
- Tue Aug 18, 10:00–11:30 ET
- Wed Aug 19, 14:00–15:30 ET
- Thu Aug 20, 09:00–10:30 ET

Attachments: redwood-workshop-agenda.pdf (draft), walkthrough-notes.md (sample prompts). Ben will own the load-test run; Marissa will lead the prompt review.

Can you confirm which slot works for the team and whether you want us to include your security contact for a quick 10-minute compliance touchpoint? I can send calendar invites and a short prep checklist once we lock a time.

Thanks,
Rachel
Rachel Kim
Principal Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
rachel.kim@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0134

From: Alex Torres <alex.torres@stargazer.ai>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 13 Aug 2026 09:25:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proof of concept workshop — interactive prompt review & load test

Thanks, Rachel — appreciate the clear agenda. Unfortunately an exec sync just popped on our calendar and we need to cancel the Tue/18 slot if that was tentatively assumed. We still want the workshop but would prefer: 

- A focused 60-minute hands-on session (prompt review + routing sanity checks) first, followed by a separate 30–45 min load run a few days later if that looks good.
- Time preferences (PT): Wed Aug 19 11:00–12:00 PT or Thu Aug 20 08:00–09:00 PT. If neither works, late afternoon PT on Thu is possible.

We also want to include our infrastructure lead (Judy Park) and security (security@stargazer.ai) on the invite. For the load test, can you share your test plan and any brief capacity expectations? We want to ensure we can allocate a staging instance and a couple of VMs for realistic traffic.

Apologies for the disruption — appreciate flexibility.

— Alex
Alex Torres
Head of Product, Stargazer AI
alex.torres@stargazer.ai | +1 (206) 555-8890

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>

Cc: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 13 Aug 2026 12:40:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Proof of concept workshop — interactive prompt review & load test

Hi Alex — thanks for the heads up and for the options. Wed 19 at 11:00 PT (that’s 14:00 ET) works for us for the 60-minute session. If that suits your team, we’ll: 

- Book a 60-minute workshop focused on prompt review and routing checks (Marissa lead)
- Schedule a separate 30–45 minute load run on Mon Aug 24 or Tue Aug 25 — Ben will coordinate the exact window and run the test from our side.

I attached the load-test-plan.csv (stub) and also uploaded the detailed test doc here: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1aBcDef-GhIjKl. The CSV has the short sample prompts we typically use and three throughput profiles (light/medium/heavy) — if you have a staging host + 2 VMs we can mirror your production-ish topology.

Quick questions:
- Do you want us to run a single model variant or do an A/B of two quantization profiles during the load run? (A/B gives more signal but needs a slightly longer window.)
- Will Judy and security@stargazer.ai join the 60-min workshop or just the load test?

Once you confirm Wed 11:00 PT, I’ll send a calendar invite and a short prep checklist (sample prompts, environment checklist). I’ve also linked this to HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/5427 (DEAL-5427) so stakeholders have visibility.

Thanks — Marissa
Marissa Cole

Request: can you send a quick reminder 24 hours before the workshop with a calendar invite and the one-page prep checklist? Also include the sample prompts we’ll be exercising so our engineers can review ahead of time.

Thanks, looking forward to it.

— Alex
